encounters.cc: Evaluation of fatigue and generalized body aches

lines: Evaluation of fatigue and generalized body aches
She works full-time in an office and reports spending little to no time outside during the day.
She lives in a northern U.S. state and says she usually wears long sleeves, pants, and sunscreen when outdoors.
On further questioning, she notes a healthy appetite and consumes a diet rich in fatty fish, which she eats multiple times a week.
She does not take any medications or supplements.
Physical examination reveals diffuse bone tenderness, especially over the shins and sternum, but no joint swelling or erythema.
Her liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits.
Radiographic imaging of the long bones shows decreased bone density and cortical thinning.
A bone biopsy reveals unmineralized osteoid with normal collagen matrix.
She is started on a supplementation regimen and referred to endocrinology for further metabolic work-up.

encounters.cc: New-onset left leg discomfort and sudden shortness of breath following cesarean delivery

lines: New-onset left leg discomfort and sudden shortness of breath following cesarean delivery

The patient is a 38-year-old woman with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension, recurrent venous thromboembolism, and endometrial hyperplasia who was evaluated one month prior for fatigue and vitamin D deficiency.
She is recovering in the hospital following an uncomplicated cesarean delivery performed two days ago.
She had been ambulating slowly with assistance but remained largely bedridden since the procedure.
On morning rounds, she complains of new-onset left leg discomfort, describing it as a sore, cramping sensation in the calf.
A few hours later, she develops sudden-onset shortness of breath while attempting to use the bathroom.
She is found sitting on the toilet, gasping for air and holding her chest.
Nurses report that she was previously alert and oriented but now appears pale and mildly confused.
Vitals reveal a heart rate of 118/min, respiratory rate of 30/min, blood pressure of 106/72 mm Hg, and oxygen saturation of 91% on room air.
On exam, she is tachypneic, anxious, and diaphoretic.
Her left leg appears mildly swollen and tender to palpation compared to the right.
Jugular venous pressure is normal, and there are no rales or wheezing on auscultation.
There is no chest wall tenderness, and heart sounds are rapid but regular.
ABG is performed to evaluate her respiratory status.

encounters.cc: Sudden-onset shortness of breath and sharp pleuritic chest pain

lines: Sudden-onset shortness of breath and sharp pleuritic chest pain
The patient with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension presents five months after her prior pulmonary embolism with sudden-onset shortness of breath.
She also reports sharp chest pain worsening when taking a deep breath.
She recently returned from a transatlantic flight and has been using oral contraceptive pills for the past year.
She denies cough, fever, or recent illness.
Respiratory rate is 24/min, heart rate is 110/min, and blood pressure is 108/72 mm Hg.
Oxygen saturation is 93% on room air
On examination, she appears mildly anxious, Cardiopulmonary examination reveals clear breath sounds and no murmurs.
There is mild tenderness in the right calf without swelling.

encounters.cc: Sudden shortness of breath and chest discomfort worsening with inspiration

lines: Sudden shortness of breath and chest discomfort worsening with inspiration

This 43-year-old female with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension and recurrent venous thromboembolism presents with sudden shortness of breath and chest discomfort worsening with inspiration.
She returned from an international flight two days ago and has been using oral contraceptive pills.
On examination, her temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 112/min, blood pressure is 108/72 mmHg, respiratory rate is 24/min, and oxygen saturation is 93% on room air.
She appears mildly anxious and is breathing rapidly.

encounters.cc: Intermittent light vaginal bleeding over the past six weeks

lines: Intermittent light vaginal bleeding over the past six weeks
The patient is a 43-year-old female with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension and recurrent venous thromboembolism who returns for evaluation of intermittent light vaginal bleeding.

She reports that her menstrual cycles had been regular while using a hormonal contraceptive for several years, but she decided to stop part of her regimen about three months ago due to perceived side effects.
Since then, her periods have become unpredictable, with occasional mid-cycle spotting.
She denies pelvic pain, discharge, or fever.
Her BMI is 23. Vital signs are normal.
Transvaginal ultrasound reveals an endometrial stripe measuring 13 mm.
Endometrial sampling is obtained and shows glandular proliferation without atypia.
